concepts_taught: free fall near Earth's surface has constant downward acceleration g when air resistance is negligible
a consistent vertical sign convention controls the signs of acceleration, displacement and velocity
released from rest means zero initial velocity, not zero acceleration
free-fall acceleration is independent of mass when air resistance is negligible
an upward launch has ascent and descent stages joined at maximum height
velocity is zero at maximum height while acceleration remains downward g
g can be measured from falling-object data using s = 1/2 gt^2 and the gradient of an s against t squared graph
skills_students_can_now_use: choose and maintain a vertical sign convention
calculate fall time, vertical displacement and impact velocity
calculate ascent time and maximum height
link ascent and descent stages through a turning point
analyse an upward launch from above ground through ascent, descent and impact
describe and process a falling-object experiment for g
interpret signed vertical results and evaluate experimental limitations
next_module_can_assume: students can analyse complete one-dimensional vertical motion under constant g
students distinguish zero velocity from zero acceleration
students can use signed constant-acceleration equations for vertical motion
students know that g is downward and independent of mass when air resistance is negligible
next_module_must_not_assume: students can separate horizontal and vertical projectile components
students know why projectile paths are parabolic
students can calculate projectile range or flight time from component motions
students can recombine perpendicular velocity components
